scope: Twelve event mappings: Delhi 2018/2021, Rajasthan six, MP two, Punjab one, Maharashtra one. Assigned government audit only; no root case table edited.
coding_rule: Use incident date, not publication date. Preserve incident-date party, coalition membership, and separate institutional police authority. Spell boundary dates are cited-source conventions and not uniformly inclusive legal timestamps; no mapped event occurs near a disputed boundary. Null end/start means not fully reconstructed or not needed, not uninterrupted incumbency.
causal_caution: Government co-occurrence is descriptive and does not establish orders, responsibility or comparative party incidence.

DL_terms.title: Delhi Legislative Assembly: About Delhi Assembly, former chief ministers
DL_terms.supports: Kejriwal is identified as AAP chief minister in 2015–2020 and 2020–2024.

DL_oath.title: Delhi Legislative Assembly: Chief Minister profile
DL_oath.supports: Kejriwal second oath 14 February 2015 and third oath 16 February 2020; AAP founder and convener.

DL_police.title: MHA Lok Sabha unstarred question 3279, 6 December 2016, p.2
DL_police.supports: Delhi Police is responsible to Parliament through the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and Lt Governor of Delhi. This is separate from the elected NCT government.

Union_PM.title: Prime Minister of India: Know the PM
Union_PM.supports: Modi served as PM in 2014–2019 and 2019–2024, leading BJP to an absolute majority at both elections.

RJ_house.title: Rajasthan Legislative Assembly: House tenure and ruling party
RJ_house.supports: 15th House: ruling INC, Ashok Gehlot; 16th House: ruling BJP, Bhajan Lal Sharma. House start dates are NOT chief-minister oath dates.

RJ_Gehlot_oath.title: Lok Sabha Secretariat, Journal of Parliamentary Information, March 2019, Rajasthan section
RJ_Gehlot_oath.supports: Ashok Gehlot was sworn in as CM on 17 December 2018. Official search-index excerpt inspected; direct PDF open timed out.

RJ_Sharma_oath.title: PMO/PIB: oath-taking of Rajasthan Chief Minister, 15 December 2023
RJ_Sharma_oath.supports: Bhajan Lal Sharma took oath as chief minister on 15 December 2023; BJP government identified.

MP_terms.title: Madhya Pradesh Assembly: Shivraj Singh Chouhan, former chief minister
MP_terms.supports: CM terms include 12 December 2008–9 December 2013 and 14 December 2013–12 December 2018; profile describes BJP career.

MP_party.title: Madhya Pradesh Assembly, 13th Assembly member profile, Budhni 156
MP_party.supports: Contemporaneous profile labels Shivraj Singh Chouhan Chief Minister and Bharatiya Janata Party.

PB_2015.title: PIB, Amritsar HRIDAY launch, 14 July 2015
PB_2015.supports: Names Parkash Singh Badal as Punjab CM and explicitly describes the SAD–BJP governing alliance. Near-contemporaneous official evidence; full legal spell boundaries not independently reconstructed.

MH_oath.title: Maharashtra Governor: oath to Uddhav Thackeray, 28 November 2019
MH_oath.supports: Governor administered oath as chief minister on 28 November 2019.

MH_2020.title: Maharashtra government DGIPR, Maharashtra Ahead, January 2020
MH_2020.supports: Contemporaneous government magazine identifies Uddhav as CM and Maha Vikas Aghadi government (printed pp.3–5); cabinet profiles explicitly list Congress, NCP and Shiv Sena party affiliations (e.g. printed pp.10,15,21). Do not substitute later party splits.

MH_ECI.title: Election Commission press note 35, 1 May 2020, hosted by Maharashtra CEO
MH_ECI.supports: Confirms Uddhav took oath on 28 November 2019; describes representations from Congress, Shiv Sena and NCP legislature parties.

MH_end.title: Maharashtra Governor photo gallery, June 2022
MH_end.supports: Dated entry 29 June 2022: CM hands over resignation to Governor.

spells.notes: End is successor oath/renewal boundary, not a finding about intra-day office holding.
Official retrospective table identifies tenure through 2024; exact terminal day not needed for July 2021 incident and not separately audited.
End denotes successor oath boundary; resignation/caretaker distinctions do not affect 2019 or 2022 events. Full support-party roster not asserted.
Official current Assembly history corroborates 2026 incumbent; null end means no later boundary needed.
Incident-date government identified; full 2012–2017 legal spell boundaries not reconstructed in this bounded primary-source audit. Official source explicitly confirms SAD–BJP alliance in July 2015.

spells.government_at_incident: Shiv Sena-led Maha Vikas Aghadi: Shiv Sena, NCP and INC
spells.notes: End is resignation date; successor took office later. Do not apply later Sena/NCP splits retrospectively.
